title: Leak-free generators
hints: Same shape as lesson 2's generator: `out := make(chan int)`, a goroutine with `defer close(out)`, then `return out`. The difference is that every blocking operation inside sits in a `select` next to `case <-ctx.Done(): return`.

`Count`: `for n := start; ; n += step { select { case out <- n: case <-ctx.Done(): return } }`. `Map` has **two** blocking operations per value, the receive from `in` and the send to `out`, so it needs two `select`s.

`Map`'s loop body: `select { case v, ok := <-in: if !ok { return }; x = v; case <-ctx.Done(): return }`, then `select { case out <- f(x): case <-ctx.Done(): return }`. A plain `for v := range in` would leak while `in` never sends.
